correctness.rationale: Every target is GL-conjugate to the nilpotent Jordan block; its centralizer has order q^(n-1)(q-1). For AB=J, rank(A) is n or n-1. These contribute GL_n choices and L*q^n choices respectively. The resulting exact T=L^2*q^(n-1)(2q-1), divided by the classical nilpotent-pair total, yields the closed conditional probability; uniform asymptotics follow by absolutely convergent product bounds. Exact enumeration corroborates; proof covers all n,q.

value.rationale: The regular nilpotent Jordan type is the natural maximal-index endpoint, a meaningful refinement of the random nilpotent-product problem. The theorem gives an exact integer pair count, a complete conditional probability across all q and n, and a strictly positive large-dimension limit at fixed field size, contrasting with exponential decay for the triangular model; this is a structural boundary rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
